name: Fish River Canyon Hiking Trail
why: Five days alone on the floor of Africa's largest canyon: sand, boulders, river crossings and hot springs at the end.
book: Book the trail with Namibia Wildlife Resorts (reservations@nwr.com.na); places sell out. Season 1 May-15 September only. Groups of at least 3, hikers over 12, each with a doctor's certificate of fitness shown at the Hobas office. Book the shuttle from Ai-Ais back to Hobas.
water: Only river pools: treat or boil it, and some pools are too salty. Carry at least 2 litres at all times; there is none on the shortcuts.
dangers: Heat: 40 °C is not rare in the canyon even in winter.
Slippery rocks and deep pools at river crossings; quicksand in the first third.
No phone signal and only a few emergency exits: one person stays with an injured hiker while another goes for help.
The first descent from the viewpoint is steep, with chains at the top.
turnaround: The last easy way out is the emergency exit near Sulphur (Palm) Springs: if anyone is struggling by then, leave there.

points.name: Hikers' Viewpoint, Hobas
points.note: Above Hell's Bend, west of Hobas. The trail drops straight down to the river, the first 100 m with chains.

points.name: Sulphur Springs (Palm Springs)
points.note: Hot sulphur springs under palms, about 17 km in: a common camp, and one of the few emergency exits out of the canyon.

points.name: |Ai-|Ais hot springs
points.note: The resort at the canyon mouth: hot spring pools, a shop and the shuttle back to Hobas.
